sections.h2: Which offices run property tax in Flagler?
sections.html:
Flagler County splits the job between its Property Appraiser, who sets value, and its Tax Collector, who mails and collects the bill. Millage is set by the levying bodies: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and others.

The Tax Collector's website, flaglertax.gov, has pages for property taxes, tangible personal property tax, tourist development tax, business tax receipts and veteran benefits. For questions about a value, an exemption or a classification, contact the Flagler County Property Appraiser directly and ask for the current forms and filing dates. Deeds are recorded, and foreclosure and tax deed auctions are run, by the circuit court clerk.

sections.h2: How are Flagler County property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Tax is billed in arrears for a calendar year, and the notice goes out around the start of November. The Tax Collector explains that the tax year runs January 1 to December 31 and payment begins November 1 of that year, and its homepage notes that real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31.

The process runs in a set order:

  • The Property Appraiser establishes values and applies exemptions to complete the tax roll.
  • The certified roll goes to the Tax Collector.
  • The Tax Collector merges in non-ad valorem assessments, which are set amounts that do not depend on value and appear on the same notice.
  • The notice is mailed to the owner's last address on the roll.

If a mortgage servicer pays from escrow, the servicer can request the bill under criteria set by the Tax Collector, and the owner gets a copy for information.

sections.h2: What is the owner's responsibility if no bill arrives in Flagler County?
sections.html:
The owner still has to pay. The Tax Collector cites section 197.122 of the Florida Statutes, which gives property owners three duties: know that taxes are due every year, find out the amount of current and delinquent tax, and pay before the delinquency date.

That means a seller who moved out, a landlord with a tenant at the address or an heir at a house with a stale mailing address should check the account rather than wait for paper. Changing the mailing address starts with the Property Appraiser's roll. Florida DOR also says unpaid taxes become delinquent April 1, and tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

sections.h2: What are the Florida property tax dates that apply in Flagler County?
sections.html:
The statewide calendar applies, with Flagler's offices handling each step locally.

Florida property tax calendar as printed by Florida DOR
DateStep
January 1Assessment date for all property
March 1Exemption and classification applications due at the Property Appraiser
April 1Tangible personal property return due (Form DR-405)
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed
Within 25 days of that noticeValue petition filed with the clerk
September to OctoberTaxing bodies hold hearings on budgets and millage
NovemberTax bills mailed, 4 percent discount in November
April 1Delinquency date
June 1Tax certificates sold by this date

DOR prints the discount ladder as 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent from November through February.

sections.h2: Can Flagler County owners spread out or defer their property tax?
sections.html:
Yes, in two situations, and both are applied for with the Tax Collector. An installment plan must be requested by the first of May in the assessment year under section 197.222, and a homestead deferral has to be filed on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year.

  • Deferral covers the tax above 5 percent of last year's household income, and all of it if household income is under $10,000.
  • A permanent resident aged 65 or older may defer the portion above 3 percent of household income.
  • Partial payments before delinquency are accepted only at the Tax Collector's discretion under section 197.374.

Ask the Flagler Tax Collector how the installment option works for your account before May 1, since the application window is fixed.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes affect a Flagler County sale?
sections.html:
Homestead and the Save Our Homes cap stay with the seller, not the house. A sale, foreclosure or other transfer of title is a change of ownership, so the parcel is reassessed at just value the next January 1 unless an exception such as a transfer between spouses applies.

While the owner holds the exemption, assessed value cannot rise by more than the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. DOR's chart lists a 2024 CPI of 3.4 percent with a 3.0 percent cap, a 2025 cap of 2.9 percent and a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent. Non-homestead property has a 10 percent annual limit on increases. If you are moving within Florida, portability lets you bring part of the cap to a new homestead, and the new home must be established inside three years counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up. Apply on Form DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1.

sections.h2: Are there veteran and senior breaks for Flagler County homeowners?
sections.html:
Florida law offers several, and the Tax Collector's veteran benefits page is a good first stop. The benefits are separate from homestead and each needs an application.

  • A disabled ex-servicemember rated 10 percent or more receives a $5,000 reduction in assessed value, not limited to homestead.
  • A veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage, which carries to an unremarried surviving spouse.
  • A deployed servicemember may qualify for an exemption equal to the share of the prior year spent deployed, on Form DR-501M.
  • A servicemember can rent out a homestead without abandoning the exemption.

Ask the Flagler County Property Appraiser which senior exemption, if any, the county has adopted.

sections.h2: What if a Flagler County parcel goes to a tax deed sale?
sections.html:
A certificate holder can apply for a tax deed two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, and the clerk then holds a public auction. The statute sets the application fee at $75, and the tax collector lists everyone who must be notified: the titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders, the party assessed and any recorded contract-for-deed buyer.

  • The winning bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater.
  • Full payment, deed stamps and recording fees follow within 24 hours, not counting weekends and holidays.
  • The certificate holder's bid accrues monthly interest at one and a half percent.
  • If nobody bids, the land goes on a list of lands available for taxes, and the county gets a 90 day window to buy it at the opening bid.

An owner who sells before the auction can pay off the certificate from the closing proceeds. Contact the Flagler Tax Collector for the redemption amount, since interest changes the figure monthly.

sections.h2: What happens to a Flagler County tax bill at closing?
sections.html:
The seller settles tax owed through closing and the title agent confirms the account before funding. The Flagler Tax Collector can tell you the balance on a parcel, and the deed stamp runs 70 cents on each $100 of price, collected by the clerk when the deed records.

If the property carries a tax certificate, the certificate holder cannot contact the owner to demand payment until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, but the lien is there from the start of delinquency. Pay it from proceeds at closing so the buyer receives clean title.

faqs.q: When does Flagler County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: Around the start of November. The Tax Collector's site says real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31, and payment begins November 1.

faqs.q: What if I never receive my Flagler County tax bill?
faqs.a: You still owe the tax. Section 197.122 puts the duty on the owner to find out the amount and pay before the delinquency date, so contact the Tax Collector and the Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: Can I defer Flagler County property tax?
faqs.a: A homestead owner can apply on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year. Deferral covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer of my Flagler County house?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1. You may be able to port part of your cap to a new Florida homestead.

faqs.q: Who sets Flagler County millage rates?
faqs.a: The levying bodies do: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and other authorities. The Property Appraiser sets value, not the rate.
